why: A machine-readable ledger so an unattended driver can take one task at a time, prove progress, and stop. Roadmap phase 4 (measurement) is the only unbuilt level; these tasks build it in the order that makes the next decision cheaper.
rules: One task per run, on its own branch plan/<id>; the driver merges to master, the session never does.
A task is done only when its acceptance is asserted by a test, a check, or a recorded measurement.
A batch without a commit, or a session that does not record a result, is blocked - silence is failure.
cargo test must pass on the branch AND after the merge.
Never publish: no gh release, no push to rust-lessons-releases, nothing that leaves the machine.
Nothing in out/ or book/book/ is hand-edited - both regenerate.

tasks.title: Every section has enough retrieval items to be scored
tasks.acceptance: Section 14 yields only two retrieval questions today, so it cannot be scored. Generate retrieval items for every section, assert a minimum of four per section in cargo test, and prove the assertion is not vacuous by removing one item and watching it fail.
tasks.note: 0.16.0. All 21 sections now yield 4 or 5 retrieval items (101 total; seventeen at five, four at four: 05, 12, 13, 15) - section 14 went 2 -> 5, section 17 3 -> 5, section 12 stayed 4 with a genuine item. MIN_QUESTIONS = 4 is one constant read by the generator and by the new test every_section_has_enough_retrieval_items_to_be_scored, which also asserts a blank per prompt, no answer visible elsewhere in the prompt, and no answer asked twice; the binary exits 1 when a section is under the floor. Non-vacuous: deleting section 05's truthiness sentence failed the test with 'section 05 yields only 3 retrieval items, below the floor of 4' and made the generator exit 1; the sentence was restored. The test found two shipping defects: emphasis stripping removed underscores inside code spans (dns_query was offered as dnsquery) and a prompt could print its own answer (section 10's FizzBuzz item). cargo test 112 tests, 111 pass, 1 ignored; mdbook build and mdbook test pass on the regenerated chapters.

tasks.title: A synthetic learner session as data, so scoring can be tested without a person
tasks.acceptance: One fixture session (answers, timings, a wrong-then-right pair) checked into the repository as data, loaded by a test, with no UI and no network. It is the input phase 4 scoring is written against.
tasks.note: 0.17.0. fixtures/session-2026-11-07-synthetic.json: 8 attempts over sections 01-03, 102400 ms on task, retrieval 4/6 and recognition 1/2, and one wrong-then-right pair (s01-q2 attempt 1 answer 'var', attempt 2 'let'). src/session.rs loads it from a string or a path, versioned schema 1, and derives correctness from answer-vs-expected instead of storing a verdict; validate() refuses an unknown schema, a section the course does not have, an attempt that does not run 1,2,3 per item, and a zero duration. tests/session_fixture.rs asserts the numbers above exactly, the pair, and that every retrieval answer is the one problems/section_NN_quiz.md gives and every recognition answer is a permutation of that section's Parsons lines. Non-vacuous, each proven by doctoring the fixture and reverting: ms 36000 -> 36001 failed 'total time on task' 102401 vs 102400; deleting the retry row failed 'exactly one item was retried, found []'; expected '2 + 3 * 4' -> '3 * 4 + 2' failed 'section 03 question 3 does not answer'. cargo test: 124 tests, 123 pass, 1 ignored. No UI, no network: the only dependency is serde/serde_json, already cached, so cargo test --offline builds.

tasks.title: Score a session: per-section correctness, time to answer, retrieval versus recognition
tasks.acceptance: Scoring reads the fixture and prints or returns a table with those three axes per section, plus an overall figure; a test asserts the numbers for the fixture exactly. This is roadmap phase 4's completion criterion, quoted in the STATE note when done.
tasks.note: 0.18.0. src/scoring.rs: score(&Session) -> Score gives every section a Tally for all tries plus separate retrieval and recognition tallies, mean and total time, items alongside tries; the overall figure is a SectionScore('overall') so one formula computes both. src/bin/score.rs prints the table (fixture by default, any path accepted, exit 2 when the loader refuses a session). tests/session_scoring.rs (7 tests) pins the fixture exactly: 01 items 3 / tries 4 / 2 right / 50.0% / 13.4 s mean / 53.7 s; 02 2/2/1/50.0%/4.7/9.4 with recognition '-'; 03 2/2/2/100.0%/19.6/39.3; overall 7/8/5/62.5%/12.8/102.4, retrieval 4/6 (66.7%), recognition 1/2 (50.0%), and each rendered row token by token. Non-vacuous: doctoring one recorded answer to 'let x = 5;' moved section 02 to 0/2 and the overall to 4/8 (50.0%) in a throwaway run, and a test asserts it. Untested mode is None printed as '-', never 0.0%, because zero of zero is unknown. Decision: tries printed beside items so a retry is visible rather than hidden in a denominator. cargo test: 137 tests, 136 passed, 1 ignored; docs quote phase 4's criterion in docs/STATE.md open item 5.

tasks.title: A source is marked read only where the note holds the evidence
tasks.acceptance: For each of the five load-bearing sources in docs/reading.md, record page or quote evidence per claim and flip skimmed to read only where that evidence exists; fix the two known citation errors with their evidence; a test asserts every 'read' entry has at least one quoted line.
tasks.note: 0.19.0. docs/reading.md now has five evidence blocks (E1-E5), each stating the page range actually looked at and quoting the source: Ericson et al. 2022 read (pp. 1-9 of 44), Haynes-Magyar 2025 read (abstract-S4.4), Margulieux & Catrambone 2016 read (pp. 58-67), Joentausta & Hellas 2018 skimmed and Kalyuga et al. 2003 skimmed - both paywalled for a stated reason, so the column still discriminates 3 read / 2 skimmed. Two known citation errors fixed with evidence (C1 wrong year 2026->ITiCSE-WGR 2022, quoted from the paper's own first page and the CrossRef record; C2 the overstated outperforms-writing-from-scratch claim, replaced by what the review says: 'no large scale attempts at replication to verify these claims', S1 p. 2) plus a third found this turn (C3 Joentausta & Hellas cited as the faded-Parsons source; it studies subgoal labels with 9-10-year-olds in LightBot, so the row now cites Weinman, Fox & Hearst, CHI 2021). Test: tests/curriculum.rs::every_read_source_has_a_quoted_line - every row marked read must carry an [En] tag resolving to a block whose Status is read, holding a Seen locator and at least one blockquote of 40+ characters, and it refuses a register that is all read or none. Non-vacuous twice: deleting E3's quoted lines failed with 'E3 is marked read and holds no quoted line - a title is not evidence', and stripping a row's tag failed with 'row says read but carries no evidence tag'; both restored. cargo test: 138 tests, 137 passing, 1 ignored. Reading changed one claim, not just footnotes: Margulieux & Catrambone found a labelled text alone did not help, so the Subgoals blocks in 07, 08, 11 and 16 are justified only beside a labelled example - queued as subgoal-example-pairing.

tasks.title: A Subgoals block travels with the labelled example that justifies it
tasks.acceptance: Margulieux & Catrambone (2016, docs/reading.md E3) found subgoal labels in expository text improved problem solving only when a worked example carried the same labels; a labelled text alone did not. Sections 07, 08, 11 and 16 carry a Subgoals block, so each needs a worked example whose steps repeat those subgoal names (or the block stops citing the finding). A test asserts that a section naming subgoals also names them inside an example, and is proven non-vacuous by removing one section's labelled example.
